page.title: Build your own Redis
page.kicker: Lecture 09 · week 5, day 1 · running case: build-your-own Redis
page.dek: Copying data out without losing it, then a cache built from one hash table up to a ring of nodes, with the cost of each decision measured in bytes, hops and data moved.
page.description: Lecture 09: meet ETL and change data capture, then build a cache like Redis on one node and make it distributed with routing, consistent hashing and replicas.

chapters.title: ETL and change data capture
chapters.summary: The blogging app's analysts need their own SQL copy of production. The obvious event pipeline drifts silently. Change data capture reads the database itself.

chapters.title: One node, every byte counted
chapters.summary: Build the cache on one machine first: a hash table, values of many types, and a hard cap on memory that the cache can always check cheaply.

chapters.title: When the cache is full: eviction and expiry
chapters.summary: Which key goes when memory runs out, and how expired keys disappear, without spending memory on bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Talking to the cache, and taking turns
chapters.summary: How other systems reach the cache (all of it is TCP; the question is the format), and how one node stays correct when two clients touch the same key.

chapters.title: Many nodes: splitting the keys and finding them
chapters.summary: One node can't take the load. Split the keys across nodes, and then decide who tells a client where its key lives.

chapters.title: Consistent hashing, DHTs and staying up
chapters.summary: Adding a node with hash % N moves half the data. Consistent hashing decides ownership so only a slice moves. Then: running it in production, its weak spots, the general idea (DHTs), and replicas.

chapters.title: What to keep
chapters.summary: The decisions, the heuristics, and where the next lessons pick up.
